newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt's CIB dividend at two pounds.
newsitem.headline: Egypt's CIB dividend at two pounds.

text.p: Egypt's retail Commercial International Bank (CIB) will give a two pound dividend per share for 1996, said corporate sources who attended the bank's annual general meeting on Thursday.
The bank has a total 50 million shares. It gave shareholders a 20 pound dividend in 1995 and in August 1996 it split its shares 1-for-10.

The sources said the payout disappointed shareholders who proposed that the bank give out a fraction of a share or more money. But the meeting voted against any increase in the dividend and the board said it wanted to retain profits for growth, the sources added.
CIB said in March it had increase net profits for calendar 1996 by almost 11 percent to 241.3 million pounds from 217.7 million in 1995.
Investment income was higher at 4.4 million from 0.28 million in 1995. The bank has also signed a three-year syndicated loan at LIBOR plus 40 basis points for $200 million.
The bank is one of the Cairo bourse's most active stocks. It issued Egypt's first global depositary receipt offering which is now trading on the SEAQ in London.
Brokers said the dividend announcement drove CIB stock prices down 3.52 pounds to 66.58 pounds.
